classification.difficultyReason: Model the building with tangent, add the flagpole to its calculated height, then use inverse tangent with the unchanged horizontal distance. Part a supplies the intermediate height.

content.prompt: From a point 100 m from the base of a building, the angle of elevation to the top of the building is $31^\circ$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How high is the building, correct to the nearest tenth of a metre?

answer.worked:
Let the building height be $h$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}\tan31^\circ&=\frac{h}{100}\\h&=100\tan31^\circ\\h&\approx60.1\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If there is a vertical flag pole of height 15 m on top of the building, what is the angle of elevation of the top of the flag pole? Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Let the required angle be $\theta$. Retain the unrounded building height from part a.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{100\tan31^\circ+15}{100}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{100\tan31^\circ+15}{100}\right)\\\theta&\approx37^\circ\end{align*}$$
